source_refs.note: 8- Peroxisomes: a main subheading of 3.4 Structure of the cell, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 74-74.

blocks.text: Peroxisomes are single membrane bounded organelles in all eukaryotic cells. These were discovered by Christian de Duve, who also discovered lysosomes.

Peroxisomes contain a variety of enzymes. Many of these enzymes are oxidative that carry out oxidation i.e. the removal of electrons and hydrogens. These enzymes primarily function to rid the cell of toxic substances. Some peroxisomes, such as those in liver cells, detoxify alcohol and other harmful compounds by carrying out their oxidation.
Some peroxisomes contain catalase enzymes, which break down hydrogen peroxide (a common by-product of cellular metabolism) into water and oxygen.

blocks.alt: A peroxisome bounded by a single membrane studded with proteins, with a granular matrix and a dark crystalline core of the enzyme urate oxidase. A magnified circle shows the membrane as a lipid bilayer.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.24: Structure of peroxisome (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 3.24).

blocks.text_alt: 2H₂O₂ (hydrogen peroxide) → 2H₂O (water) + O₂ (oxygen), with catalase over the arrow

blocks.text: Defects in peroxisomes cause a number of metabolic disorders. The most serious of these disorders is Zellweger syndrome, which is characterized by absence or reduced number of peroxisomes in the cells. It is congenital disorder (present at birth) and has no cure or effective treatment and usually causes death within the first year of life.
